reviews.narrative: FY2026 annual credit review of the Blue Ridge relationship, prepared against the 15 February 2027 review date and brought forward by the overdue Q2 2026 debt service certificate. Grade affirmed at 4.
reviews.summary: Blue Ridge group: $27.75MM committed across seven booked facilities in three packages, $24.6MM outstanding. The practice package carries a $3.0MM receivables revolver, the $6.5MM Skyland acquisition term loan and a $1.8MM imaging note. The real estate package carries the $9.2MM medical office building mortgage and the $2.1MM parking structure loan at Blue Ridge Medical Properties LLC. The surgery centre package carries the $4.4MM build-out loan and a $750K equipment note at the 51 percent owned joint venture. All four physician partners guarantee every facility on a limited, several basis at 25 percent of each note.
reviews.recommendation: Affirm grade 4 and renew the $3.0MM revolving line at WSJ Prime plus 0.50 percent at its January 2028 maturity. Obtain the Q2 2026 debt service certificate within thirty days and reinstate quarterly reporting discipline. Hold the capex exception as mitigated rather than waived, and raise the annual capex limit to $2.0MM at renewal to match the imaging plan.
reviews.riskComments: Risk grade affirmed at 4. Coverage of 1.41x at the last measured quarter and fixed charge coverage of 1.34x are both inside covenant. The only open items are the FY2026 capex breach, mitigated, and the overdue Q2 2026 certificate, which is a reporting failure rather than a performance one.
reviews.strengths: Twenty eight year operating history and stable partner group with no departures since 2019. Owner-occupied real estate held in an affiliate with $1.1MM of equity above the mortgages at the March 2026 appraisal. Ancillary revenue from imaging, physical therapy and the surgery centre distribution diversifies away from professional fees. Payor mix weighted to commercial rather than government.
reviews.weaknesses: Reporting discipline: the Q2 2026 debt service certificate is twenty days late and the practice management conversion is the stated cause. Capital expenditure ran $370K over the covenant limit in FY2026. Physician concentration, with the top two surgeons generating 41 percent of professional revenue. The surgery centre is 49 percent owned by a hospital system whose intentions on renewal of the joint venture agreement in 2029 are not known.

riskRatingReviews.comments: Annual risk rating review supporting the FY2026 annual review. Computed grade 4 on coverage of 1.41x, leverage of 1.7x and twenty eight years of partner management. No override requested. The overdue Q2 certificate is treated as a reporting item and does not move the grade.
